(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2020 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2020]]) * First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2020) * Third-team All-Big 12 (2019) * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Freshman Team (2019) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018]]) }} '''Devon Durrell Dotson''' (born August 2, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. ==High school career== Dotson attended [[Providence Day School]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]], along with [[Grant Williams (basketball)|Grant Williams]] and Joshua Howard, graduating in 2018. During his senior year of high school, Dotson averaged 28.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 5.1 assists, leading the school to its sixth conference title.{{cite web|url=https://kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=15555|title=Men's Basketball Roster – Kansas Jayhawks|website=Kansas Jayhawks|date=June 27, 2018|publisher=KU Athletic Dept.|access-date=April 6, 2019}} Devon scored 2,607 points becoming the school's all-time leader in points. Devon was a 4 Time All-Conference and 3 Time All-State Selection. He was also a 2-time Charlotte Observer All-Mecklenburg boys' basketball player of the year. Devon ended his high school career by being selected and playing in the 2018 [[McDonald's All-American Game]] held in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article207576654.html|title=McDonald's All-American Devon Dotson repeats as All-Mecklenburg Player of the Year|work=charlotteobserver|access-date=November 27, 2018|language=en}} ===Recruiting=== On October 13, 2017, Dotson committed to playing [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Kansas]], choosing the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Jayhawks]] over offers from [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|UNC]], and other schools.{{cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/the-devon-dotson-blog-ok-so-heres-why-i-chose-kansas|title=Devon basketball|Jayhawks]] starting point guard playing national ranked [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]] in the 2018 Champions Classic on November 6, 2018. In his first collegiate game, Dotson pitched in 16 points and three steals, showcasing his quickness with a number of layups.{{Cite news|url=https://www.cjonline.com/sports/20181106/frosh-frenzy-quentin-grimes-devon-dotson-power-ku-basketball-to-92-87-win-over-no-10-michigan-state|title=Frosh frenzy: Quentin Grimes, Devon Dotson power KU basketball to 92–87 win over No. 10 Michigan State|last=Galloway|first=Matt|work=The Topeka Capital|access-date=November 27, 2018|language=en}} Dotson was on the watch list for the 2019 [[Bob Cousy Award|Bob Cousy Point Guard of the Year Award]], the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame]] announced on October 15, 2018.Bedore, Gary. [https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article220061835.html KU’s Devon Dotson one of 20 players on Cousy list; Big 12/Big East challenge in works?], ''[[Kansas City Star]]'', October 15, 2018. Retrieved January 17, 2019. In his [[2018–19 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2018–19 freshman season]], Dotson averaged 12.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and 1.4 steals a game while shooting 36.3% from three-point territory.[https://kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=15555 2018–19 Men's Basketball Roster – 11 Devon Dotson], KU Athletics.com. Retrieved April 6, 2019. On February 11, 2019, Dotson led the Jayhawks to a win in overtime against the [[TCU Horned Frogs]] in [[Fort Worth, Texas]], by scoring 25 points, grabbing 10 rebounds, and passing for 5 assists with 6 turnovers in 45 minutes of playing time.Newell, Jesse. [https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article226128275.html ‘There was no choice’: How Devon Dotson delivered when KU needed him most], ''[[Kansas City Star]]'', February 12, 2019. Retrieved February 12, 2019. On February 13, 2019, Dotson was named national freshman of the week by [[CBS Sports]] and the [[U.S. Basketball Writers Association]] for his play in the TCU game among others.Tait, Matt. [http://www2.kusports.com/news/2019/feb/13/national-honor-latest-indictator-freshman-point-gu/ National honor the latest indicator of freshman point guard Devon Dotson’s rapid development], ''[[Lawrence Journal-World]]'', February 13, 2019. Retrieved February 13, 2019. During his sophomore season, Dotson scored a career-high 31 points in a 90–84 overtime win over [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] on November 27.{{cite news |title=No. 4 Kansas beats Dayton 90–84 in overtime for Maui title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401182629 |access-date=November 27, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 27, 2019}} He was named co-MVP of the Maui Jim Maui Invitational and was named Big 12 player of the week on December 2.{{cite web|url=https://big12sports.com/news/2019/12/2/dotson-tshiebwe-collect-mens-basketball-awards.aspx|title=Dotson & Tshiebwe Collect Men's Basketball Awards|publisher=Big 12 Conference|date=December 2, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} Dotson missed a game against [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] on January 14, 2020, with a hip injury.{{cite news |title=Hip pointer shelves leading scorer Devon Dotson for No. 6 Kansas |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28486048/hip-pointer-shelves-leading-scorer-devon-dotson-no-6-kansas |access-date=January 15, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=January 14, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Dotson was named to the First Team All-Big 12.{{cite press release|url=https://big12sports.com/news/2020/3/7/mens-basketball-all-big-12-awards-announced.aspx|title=Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced|work=[[Big 12 Conference]]|date=March 8, 2020 |access-date=March 8, 2020}} He averaged 18.1 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game as a sophomore.{{cite news |last1=Dauster |first1=Rob |title=NBC Sports College Basketball All-American Teams |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/03/10/college-basketball-all-american-teams/ |access-date=March 16, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 10, 2020}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] and hired an agent. After going undrafted, Dotson signed with the Chicago Bulls.{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Kansas' Devon Dotson decides to enter NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29030385/kansas-devon-dotson-decides-enter-nba-draft |access-date=April 13, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 13, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2020–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Dotson signed with his hometown team the [[Chicago Bulls]], on a [[two-way contract]] with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite news |last1=Schaefer |first1=Rob |title=Bulls signing Kansas guard Devon Dotson to two-way deal |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/report-bulls-signing-kansas-guard-devon-dotson-undrafted-free-agent |access-date=November 19, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=November 19, 2020}} As the Windy City Bulls opted out of the 2020–21 G League season, Dotson was assigned to the [[Canton Charge]], making his debut in their season opener on February 11, 2021. On August 19, 2021, the Bulls announced that they had re-signed Dotson to a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Bulls sign free agents Bradley, Green, and Dotson|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-free-agents-bradley-green-and-dotson|website=NBA.com|date=August 19, 2021|access-date=August 19, 2021}} During the 2021–22 season, Dotson appeared in 11 games with the Bulls and averaged 2.6 points and 1.4 assists per game. On January 16, 2022, he was waived by the Bulls.{{Cite web|title=BULLS WAIVE DEVON DOTSON|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-devon-dotson|url-status=live|access-date=January 17, 2022|website=NBA.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220117171416/https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-devon-dotson |archive-date=January 17, 2022 }} ===Windy City Bulls (2022)=== On January 22, 2022, Dotson was re-acquired by the [[Windy City Bulls]]. However, he was waived on February 4.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 24, 2022|access-date=January 24, 2022}} Three days later, Dotson was re-acquired by the Bulls.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 7, 2022|access-date=February 7, 2022}} ===Capital City Go-Go / Washington Wizards (2022–2024)=== [[File:Devon Dotson watching intensely.jpg|thumb|left|Devon Dotson intensely watching the huddle during a timeout at a Capital City Go Go game]] On August 25, 2022, Dotson was traded to the [[Capital City Go-Go]]{{cite web|title=2022-2023 Capital City Go-Go Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Capital-City-Go-Go/55/Transaction_History/2023|website=RealGM.com|access-date=October 21, 2023}} and on November 20, he signed a two-way contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|first=Jackson|last=Filyo|title=Wizards sign Devon Dotson to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-devon-dotson-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=November 20, 2022|access-date=November 20, 2022}} However, on January 17, 2023, he was waived{{Cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Wizards Waive Guard Devon Dotson|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/01/wizards-waive-guard-devon-dotson.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=January 17, 2023|access-date=January 18, 2023}} and two days later, he was reacquired by the Go-Go. On October 19, 2023, Dotson re-signed with the Wizards,{{cite tweet|author=Washington Wizards|title=Official: We have signed Devon Dotson to an Exhibit 10 contract. We have also waived Jules Bernard.|number=1715061519132537083|user=WashWizards|date=October 19, 2023|access-date=October 21, 2023}} but was waived the next day.{{cite tweet|author=Washington Wizards|title=Official: We have waived Devon Dotson and Michael Foster Jr.|number=1715593260997984687|user=WashWizards|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 21, 2023}} On October 30, he returned to Capital City{{cite web|title=Go-Go Announce Training Camp Roster, Dates|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-training-camp-roster-dates|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 26, 2023}} and on March 15, 2024, he was bought out by the Go-Go.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Capital City Go-Go Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Capital-City-Go-Go/55/Transaction-History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 15, 2024}} ===Spain (2024–2025)=== On March 18, 2024, Dotson signed with [[Obradoiro CAB|Monbus Obradoiro]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web|title=El Monbus Obradoiro incorpora a Devon Dotson|url=https://www.obradoirocab.com/publicaciones/el-monbus-obradoiro-incorpora-a-devon-dotson/177790/|website=ObradoiroCAB.com|date=March 18, 2024|access-date=March 18, 2024|language=Spanish}} On July 16, 2024, he signed for another Liga ACB team, [[Joventut Badalona]]. Dotson signed a two season contract.{{cite web|title=Devon Dotson: un base elèctric i amb molts punts a les mans|url=https://www.penya.com/ca/club/noticies/173-2024-2025/4430-devon-dotson-un-base-electric-i-amb-molts-punts-a-les-mans|website=penya.com|date=July 16, 2024|access-date=July 10, 2025|language=ca}} On June 28, 2025, Joventut announced Dotson was leaving the team after activating his contract's release clause.{{cite web|title=Comunicat oficial: Devon Dotson |url=https://www.penya.com/ca/club/noticies/173-2024-2025/4918-comunicat-oficial-devon-dotson|website=penya.com|date=June 28, 2025|access-date=July 10, 2025|language=ca}} ===Beşiktaş (2025–present)=== On July 13, 2025, Dotson signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Gain]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]].{{cite web|title=Devon Dotson Beşiktaş web|url=http://www2.kusports.com/weblogs/tale-tait/2017/sep/15/in-home-visit-with-5-star-pg-devon-dotso/|title=In-home visit with 5-star PG Devon Dotson 'great,' according to Dotson's father {{!}}
